\caption{Event-study coefficients, log cell employment, eleven countries pooled}

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.92\textwidth]{\tabfig/emp_index_q5_panel.png}
\caption{Employment by quintile of generative-AI exposure, 2022 $=$ 100, by country and pooled}
\label{fig:index}
\floatfoot{\footnotesize \textit{Notes:} Employment summed over all cells in the quintile, divided by its 2022 mean. Quintiles are employment-weighted at the 2022 baseline and defined at each country's cell digit level; quintile 5 is the most exposed. The pooled series is the employment-weighted mean of the country indices over the countries observed in each quarter. Bolivia and Georgia have few cells and noisy indices.}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{\tabfig/itbpo_by_country.png}
\caption{IT and business-process services: employment and under-25 share, annual averages}
\label{fig:youthshare}
\floatfoot{\footnotesize \textit{Notes:} Sector $=$ ISIC Rev.\ 4 divisions 62 (computer programming and consultancy), 63 (information services) and 82 (office and business support, including call centres); South Africa 62 only; Mexico ENOE code 5611. Top row: employment in the sector, in its clerical and service occupations (ISCO 4 and 5) and in the whole economy, indexed to 2022. Bottom row: under-25 share of sector employment against the economy-wide share. Annual averages of quarters; the latest year may be partial. Bolivia (290 sector workers in 2022) and Georgia (92) are too small for the share to be reliable.}
\end{figure}
